A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete 33-page texts, equations, figures, references and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-data simulations validating theoretical predictions, including repeated experiments in Figures 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and adds covariance experiments, image-derived evaluations and a neural-network experiment in Figures 3, 10 and 11.

M1.justification: The central linear robust-ERM framework remains. Appendix B.3 adds a bounded procedural extension using a two-layer ReLU estimator and projected-gradient attacks enforcing the orthogonality constraint. This supplements the linear analysis rather than replacing its main estimator.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian settings. v2 additionally uses MNIST 0-versus-1 and Fashion-MNIST sandals-versus-ankle-boots images, transformed into random Fourier features with teacher-generated labels. Figure 3 also extends evaluated input conditions to Gaussian covariates with power-law covariance spectra.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons between consistent and unrestricted attacks, attack geometries, and the no-features control remain. The new neural-network experiment tests whether the findings extend beyond linear estimators; it does not introduce a competing baseline into the existing method comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation definitions replace target-probability invariance with target-score invariance. Added protocols include 1,000 test samples for image-derived evaluations and a 20% validation split with 50-step, five-restart PGD for the MLP. The relocated existence comparison changes its stated regularization from 10^-3 in v1 Figure 3 left to 10^-2 in v2 Figure 8 left; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds covariance sensitivity analysis comparing low-rank and tail-aligned predictors at fixed target alignment, and a nonlinear-estimator experiment testing whether the observed trends depend on linearity. These extend the retained alternative-feature-map and boundary-error analyses substantially.

E5.justification: Both versions use repeated simulations with 10-realization averages and standard-deviation error bars. The new image and MLP results follow this existing reporting practice. No increased repetition count, confidence-interval procedure or significance-testing method is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds findings on covariance alignment, image-derived data and nonlinear estimators. Figure 10 reports sample-complexity-dependent consistent robust-error trends, while Figure 11 reports opposite boundary- and robust-error trends for the MLP. The latent-space attack-existence curves in v1 Figure 4 left are removed; its remaining error panels reappear in v2 Figure 9.

T1.justification: v2 revises consistency definitions, signed-margin formulas, latent attack-surface expressions and self-consistent equations. It generalizes Gaussian existence probabilities to arbitrary covariance, supplies a Gaussian-specific proof of the robust-error lower bound, and adds Proposition 4.11 with an extreme-overparameterization derivation in Appendix C.4. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace the earlier directional account of overparameterization with a metric- and regime-dependent claim, including eventual reversal of the finite-range trends. The formal scope of consistency also narrows to score-preserving perturbations, with implications for claims about label-preserving vulnerability.

C2.justification: v2 explains that score preservation is stronger than label preservation and that its metrics therefore lower-bound label-preserving vulnerability. It adds algorithmic-versus-statistical irreducibility, covariance-alignment interpretations, and explicit limitations concerning Gaussian proportional asymptotics and the absence of feature learning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link and substantial implementation information for the new experiments: image centering, Fourier-feature construction, teacher fitting, optimizer settings, early stopping and projected attacks. It also corrects optimizer references and explicitly describes joint two-dimensional tuning of the training budget and regularization parameter.

R1.justification: The brief related-work discussion becomes a substantially expanded Appendix A explaining distinctions from earlier robust-generalization, consistency and latent-model analyses. New discussions include reliable learning, missing-data regression and adversarial distillation. Publication updates to already-cited works are separate from these substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: The prose and organization are extensively revised. Related work moves to Appendix A, finite-dimensional proofs are consolidated in Appendix C, the replica derivation is shortened, and explanatory remarks and explicit limitations reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to a two-column conference layout. v2 adds a geometric diagram, covariance panel and image/MLP figures, and reorganizes existing plots across Figures 4, 8 and 9. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects important definition and signed-margin problems, adds relevant validation, and improves reproducibility information. However, its replacement latent-model characterization is internally inconsistent: Equation (22) and Theorem 4.8's definitions imply tau = 2P when gamma > 1, whereas Equation (25) gives tau = P. The PDFs do not establish whether this is merely a display error or affects calculations. These substantial gains and unresolved theoretical concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
